item.title: GraphMind: From Operational Traces to Self-Evolving Workflow Automation
item.description:
GraphMind solves the problem of automating complex operational workflows by building a system that constructs, executes, and evolves action-centric workflow graphs with minimal human effort. The researchers built a system that extracts workflow graphs from operational traces and adapts over time. The result is a self-evolving workflow automation system that can automate tasks with minimal human input.

IT Breakdown: If you manage workflow automation, here is what to do: review your current automation systems to see if they can be improved with GraphMind's self-evolving workflow graphs, assess the potential for adapting GraphMind to your organisation's specific workflow needs, and consider implementing GraphMind to reduce manual effort and improve automation efficiency.

item.title: [News] Glean’s top line crosses $300M as AI budget-cutting becomes its major selling point
item.description: Glean's top line crosses $300M as AI budget-cutting becomes its major selling point. This is likely driven by tech giants like Google and Microsoft increasing their AI investments, making Glean's focus on budget-cutting a selling point.

item.title: [News] The internet is being rebuilt for machines
item.description: AWS and Cloudflare are redesigning cloud infrastructure to account for machine-generated internet traffic. This shift is driven by AI agents moving from experiments to production.

item.title: [News] MUFG aims to become AI-native with OpenAI
item.description: MUFG is using OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise to become AI-native, improve workflows, and deliver new AI-powered financial services. This aims to transform MUFG's organizational structure, employee roles, and service offerings.

item.title: [News] Asana acquires no-code agent-builder StackAI
item.description: Asana acquired no-code agent-builder StackAI, a startup that generates chatbots and AI agents. This means Asana can now more easily integrate AI into its workflow tools, which may impact how IT teams use the platform.

item.title: [News] Researchers automated LLM reasoning strategy design and cut token usage by 69.5%
item.description: Researchers from Meta, Google, and several universities introduced AutoTTS, a framework that automates large language models' reasoning strategy design, achieving a 69.5% reduction in token usage. This breakthrough can lead to significant improvements in models' computational efficiency and reduce inference costs.
